examples.en: The revised edition of the dictionary came out this month.
Many new words were added in the revised edition.
The teacher told us to use the revised textbook.
The revised edition and the first edition have different page counts.

examples.ko: 저자가 십 년 만에 개정판을 냈어요.
examples.en: The author put out a revised edition after ten years.

examples.ko: 이 책은 두 번째 개정판이라서 내용이 더 정확해요.
examples.en: This is the second revised edition, so the content is more accurate.

explain: 책의 판은 '초판', '개정판', '증보판'처럼 불러요. 개정판은 틀린 곳을 고치거나 새 내용을 넣었을 때, 증보판은 내용을 늘렸을 때 많이 써요. 서점에서는 '개정판 출간'이라고 광고해요.
explain_en: Book editions are called things like '초판', '개정판', and '증보판'. A 개정판 corrects mistakes or adds new content, while a 증보판 expands it. Bookstores advertise a new one as '개정판 출간'.

examples.en: I went to the baseball park at the weekend.

examples.ko: 새 구장이 다음 달에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: The new ballpark opens next month.
We agreed to meet in front of the stadium.
The grass at this ballpark is really beautiful.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에는 작은 축구 구장이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small football ground in our neighbourhood.

examples.ko: 구장 안에서 먹는 치킨이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: Chicken eaten inside the ballpark tastes best.

explain: 구장은 야구나 축구처럼 공으로 하는 경기를 하는 곳이에요. 한국에서는 특히 야구장을 말할 때 많이 써서 '잠실 구장'처럼 불러요. 축구는 '축구장'이나 '경기장'이라고도 하고, 아주 큰 경기장은 '스타디움'이라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: Gujang is a place where ball games such as baseball or football are played. In Korea it is used especially for baseball parks, as in 잠실 구장. Football grounds are also called 축구장 or 경기장, and very large ones 스타디움.

examples.en: Busan is an international city with a port.
Many foreigners live in this international city.
As an international city, it has restaurants from many countries.
This area was developed as an international city.
My dream is to work in an international city.
To become an international city, transportation must be convenient.

explain: 외국인과 외국 회사가 많고 세계와 활발히 교류하는 도시를 말해요. '국제도시답게', '국제도시로 발전하다'처럼 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '글로벌 도시'도 들려요.
explain_en: It describes a city with many foreigners and foreign companies and active exchange with the world. Common uses are '국제도시답게' and '국제도시로 발전하다'. You may also hear '글로벌 도시'.

examples.en: The government came up with a new countermeasure.

examples.ko: 이번 사고에 대한 대응책 마련이 시급해요.
examples.en: Preparing a response to this accident is urgent.
I can't think of a good countermeasure.
What are you thinking of as a countermeasure?

examples.ko: 이 대응책은 비용이 너무 많이 들어요.
examples.en: This countermeasure costs too much.

examples.ko: 미리 대응책을 알아 두면 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: If you know the countermeasures in advance, you feel at ease.

explain: '대책'이라고도 해요. 보통 '대응책을 세우다/마련하다/내놓다'처럼 써요. 문제나 상대의 움직임에 맞서서 하는 방법이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: People also say '대책'. It is usually used as '대응책을 세우다/마련하다/내놓다'. It carries the feeling of a method to face a problem or another party's actions.

examples.en: My English reading score went up a lot.
Reading comprehension questions take a long time.
I practice Korean reading comprehension every day.

examples.ko: 이 글은 독해가 어려워서 몇 번 읽었어요.
examples.en: This text is hard to follow, so I read it several times.

examples.ko: 독해력을 키우려면 책을 많이 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To build reading comprehension, you have to read many books.
The reading passage on the exam was too long.

explain: '독해'는 주로 시험이나 공부에서 글을 읽고 내용을 이해하는 영역을 말해요. '읽기'는 소리 내어 읽는 것까지 포함하지만 독해는 내용 이해와 문제 풀이에 더 가까워요. '독해력', '독해 문제', '독해 지문'처럼 이어서 써요.
explain_en: 독해 is mainly the area of reading a text and understanding its content in exams or study. 읽기 can include reading aloud, but 독해 is closer to understanding content and solving questions. It goes in compounds like 독해력, 독해 문제 and 독해 지문.

examples.en: This chair has a high backrest, so it's comfortable.
May I tilt the backrest back a little?

examples.ko: 등받이 없는 의자에 오래 앉으면 허리가 아파요.
examples.en: Sitting a long time on a chair without a backrest hurts my back.

examples.ko: 차 등받이 각도를 바꿨더니 자세가 편해졌어요.
examples.en: I changed the angle of the car seat back and my posture got more comfortable.
I put a cushion against the backrest.
The backrest moves when you pull the handle.

explain: 의자나 자동차 좌석에서 등을 기대는 부분이에요. 팔을 올리는 '팔걸이'와 같이 의자 부분 이름으로 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is the part of a chair or car seat you lean your back against. It is good to learn it together with '팔걸이' (armrest) as chair-part names.

en: to be infinite; to be limitless; to be endless

examples.en: The universe looks infinite.
Children's imagination is limitless.
I am grateful to my parents for their boundless love.
The possibilities are endless, so don't give up.

examples.ko: 자원이 무한하지 않아서 아껴 써야 해요.
examples.en: Resources are not unlimited, so we must save them.

examples.ko: 무한할 것 같던 에너지가 어느새 다 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The energy that seemed endless ran out before I knew it.

explain: 반대말은 '유한하다'인데 일상에서는 잘 쓰지 않고, 보통 '끝이 없다', '한이 없다'라고 말해요. '무한한 사랑', '무한한 가능성'처럼 명사 앞에 오는 모양이 많아요. 식당 간판의 '무한 리필'에서도 자주 봐요.
explain_en: The opposite is '유한하다', but it is rarely used in daily life; people usually say '끝이 없다' (there is no end). It often appears before nouns, as in '무한한 사랑' (boundless love) or '무한한 가능성'. You also see it on restaurant signs as '무한 리필' (unlimited refills).

examples.en: I hike every Sunday.
We started hiking at dawn.
It is raining, so we are not hiking today.
I took many photos while hiking with friends.

examples.ko: 겨울에 산행할 때는 따뜻하게 입어야 해요.
examples.en: When hiking in winter, you should dress warmly.
Yesterday I went hiking on Seoraksan.

explain: '등산하다'와 비슷하지만 말투가 조금 더 글 같아요. 보통은 '산에 가다', '등산하다'라고 하고, '산행하다'는 산악회 후기나 방송에서 들어요. '설악산을 산행하다'처럼 산 이름을 목적어로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Similar to '등산하다' but a bit more written in tone. People usually say '산에 가다' or '등산하다'; '산행하다' appears in hiking-club reports and broadcasts. The mountain name can be the object: '설악산을 산행하다'.

examples.en: When I am in a big hurry, I skip the greeting.
The explanation was too long, so I left out the middle.

examples.ko: 발표할 때 이 부분은 생략해도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: It is fine to skip this part when you present.

examples.ko: 한국어에서는 주어를 자주 생략할 수 있어요.
examples.en: In Korean, you can often omit the subject.
Skipping the procedure became a problem.
I wrote the omitted word inside parentheses.

explain: 한국어는 '(나는) 밥 먹었어요'처럼 주어를 생략하는 일이 아주 많아요. 글에서 중간 내용을 줄일 때 쓰는 점 세 개 '…'는 '말줄임표'라고 해요.
explain_en: Korean often drops the subject, as in '(나는) 밥 먹었어요'. The three dots '…' used to shorten the middle of a text are called '말줄임표'.

en: holy place; sacred site; mecca (for fans)

examples.en: Jerusalem is a holy place for several religions.

examples.ko: 순례자들이 성지를 찾아 먼 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: Pilgrims walked a long way to visit the holy site.

examples.ko: 그 카페는 드라마 팬들의 성지가 됐어요.
examples.en: That cafe has become a mecca for drama fans.

examples.ko: 이 야구장은 팬들에게 성지 같은 곳이에요.
examples.en: This ballpark is like a holy ground to fans.
After the pilgrimage, my mind felt at ease.

examples.ko: 산 위에 있는 성지에는 조용한 분위기가 흘러요.
examples.en: A quiet atmosphere fills the sacred site on the mountain.

explain: 종교에서 거룩하게 여기는 곳을 말해요. 요즘은 팬들 사이에서 '드라마 촬영지', '유명 가수의 가게'처럼 꼭 한 번 가 봐야 하는 곳을 '성지'라고도 불러요. 이때는 장난스럽고 가벼운 말이라 친구들끼리 편하게 써요. 같이 쓰는 말은 '성지 순례'예요.

phrases.example: 주말에 드라마 촬영지로 성지 순례를 다녀왔어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팬이 좋아하는 작품이나 사람과 관련된 장소를 일부러 찾아다니는 일을 장난스럽게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful way of describing fans deliberately visiting places linked to a work or person they love.

explain_en: Originally a place that a religion regards as holy. Among fans it also means a must-visit place such as a drama filming location or a famous singer's shop, in a playful, light tone used between friends. A common pairing is 성지 순례 (pilgrimage, or a fan trip to such places).

en: to be vital; to be essential; to be indispensable

examples.en: It's handy to have emergency medicine at home.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 보조 배터리가 요긴하게 쓰였어요.
examples.en: The portable battery came in very handy on the trip.
Thank you for telling me such useful information.

examples.ko: 요긴할 때 쓰려고 돈을 조금 모아 뒀어요.
examples.en: I saved a little money to use when it's really needed.
This app is more useful than I thought.

examples.ko: 갑자기 비가 와서 우산이 요긴했던 하루였어요.
examples.en: It was a day when an umbrella came in handy because it suddenly rained.

explain: '중요하다'와 달리 필요한 때에 꼭 쓸모가 있다는 느낌이에요. 물건, 정보, 돈에 많이 쓰고 '요긴하게 쓰다'로 자주 말해요. 거창한 일보다 생활 속 쓸모를 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: Unlike '중요하다' (important), it has the feeling of being truly useful at the moment you need it. It is often used for objects, information and money, as in '요긴하게 쓰다' (put to good use). It fits practical everyday usefulness rather than grand matters.

examples.ko: 동생은 키가 요만할 때부터 피아노를 쳤어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling played piano from when they were only this tall.

examples.ko: 요만한 상자에 이 물건이 다 들어가요?
examples.en: Does all of this fit in a box this size?
The baby's hand is this small, so it's really cute.

examples.ko: 문제가 요만하니 너무 걱정하지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: The problem is only this big, so you don't need to worry too much.
Would a gift this size be enough for my friend?

examples.ko: 처음 만났을 때 아이는 요만했는데 벌써 고등학생이에요.
examples.en: When we first met, the child was this small, and now they're already in high school.

explain: 손짓으로 크기를 보여 주며 '요만한 상자'처럼 말할 때 자주 써요. '이만하다'보다 작고 귀여운 느낌이 있어요. 크기뿐 아니라 '요만하면 됐어요'처럼 정도에도 쓰고, 보통 '요만한 N' 꼴로 나와요.
explain_en: People often say it with a hand gesture to show size, as in '요만한 상자'. It feels smaller and cuter than '이만하다'. It can also express degree, as in '요만하면 됐어요', and usually appears as '요만한 + noun'.

examples.ko: 자전거 체인에 윤활유를 발랐더니 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: After I put lubricant on the bicycle chain, it stopped making noise.
The door was squeaking, so I sprayed lubricant on the hinges.

examples.ko: 윤활유가 떨어지면 기계가 고장 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the lubricant runs out, the machine can break down.

examples.ko: 자동차 윤활유는 정기적으로 갈아 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You need to change a car's lubricating oil regularly.

examples.ko: 이 스프레이는 윤활유 역할을 해서 나사가 잘 풀려요.
examples.en: This spray works as a lubricant, so the screws come loose easily.

examples.ko: 윤활유 한 방울만 넣어도 훨씬 부드러워요.
examples.en: Even one drop of lubricant makes it much smoother.

explain: 기계나 문이 부드럽게 움직이도록 바르는 기름이에요. '기름'보다 정확한 말이고, 정비나 수리 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 사람 사이를 부드럽게 해 주는 것을 비유로도 말해요.

phrases.example: 작은 칭찬은 사람 사이의 윤활유 같아요.
phrases.en: Small compliments are like a lubricant between people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 사이를 부드럽게 해 주는 것을 비유할 때 써요. 유머, 대화, 칭찬 같은 말과 함께 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for something that makes relationships run smoothly. It appears with words like humor, conversation and compliments.

explain_en: It is the oil applied so machines or doors move smoothly. It is more specific than '기름' and often comes up when talking about maintenance and repairs. It is also used figuratively for whatever smooths things between people.

examples.en: My pitch keeps going off when I sing.
I practice matching the pitch every day.

examples.ko: 기타 음정이 맞지 않으면 소리가 이상해요.
examples.en: If the guitar isn't in tune, it sounds odd.

examples.ko: 음정과 박자를 둘 다 지키기가 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to keep both pitch and rhythm.
In a choir, the pitches have to match each other.

examples.ko: 높은 음정은 목에 힘이 많이 들어가요.
examples.en: High pitches take a lot of effort in the throat.

explain: 노래에서 '음정'은 소리의 높낮이가 맞는지를, '박자'는 시간에 맞게 부르는지를 가리켜요. '음정이 틀리다', '음정이 안 맞다', '음정을 맞추다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In singing, 음정 is whether the pitch is right, and 박자 is whether it is on time. Typical phrases are '음정이 틀리다', '음정이 안 맞다' and '음정을 맞추다'.

examples.en: The kids keep waiting impatiently for Dad to come.
I'm anxiously waiting, hour by hour, for news of whether I passed.

examples.ko: 이제나저제나 하며 문자를 기다렸는데 안 왔어요.
examples.en: I kept waiting for a text, thinking it would come any moment, but it never did.

examples.ko: 그는 이제나저제나 연락이 올까 휴대폰만 봤어요.
examples.en: He just kept staring at his phone, wondering if a call would come any minute.

examples.ko: 버스가 이제나저제나 오나 하고 계속 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: I kept looking down the road, wondering when the bus would finally come.
Grandmother is waiting eagerly for her grandchild to arrive.

explain: 거의 항상 '기다리다'와 함께 써서, 언제 올까 조마조마하며 계속 기다리는 마음을 나타내요. 그냥 '기다리다'보다 초조하고 간절한 느낌이 더 커요. 주로 뒤에 '-나 하고' 같은 표현이 이어져요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with '기다리다' and shows the nervous feeling of waiting and wondering when something will come. It sounds more anxious and eager than plain '기다리다'. It is often followed by patterns like '-나 하고'.

examples.ko: 우리 지역구 국회의원은 다음 주에 시장을 방문해요.
examples.en: Our district's lawmaker will visit the market next week.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 지역구 주민을 자주 만나요.
examples.en: That lawmaker often meets residents of the district.
The district changed, so the polling place is different.
He won in his district three times in a row.

examples.ko: 저는 지역구 후보와 비례대표 후보에게 각각 투표했어요.
examples.en: I voted separately for a district candidate and a proportional candidate.

examples.ko: 지역구의 오랜 숙원 사업이 드디어 시작됐어요.
examples.en: The district's long-awaited project has finally started.

explain: 지역구는 '비례대표'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 지역구는 우리 동네 사람을 뽑고, 비례대표는 정당을 보고 뽑아요. 뉴스에서 '지역구 의원'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 지역구 often appears as a pair with 비례대표. With 지역구 you elect a person for your own area, while with 비례대표 you vote by party. In the news you see phrases like 지역구 의원.

examples.en: I poured hot tea into the teacup.
The teacup I got as a gift is so pretty.
I dropped the teacup and it broke.
I carefully placed the teacup in front of the guest.
A flower petal is floating in the teacup.
This teacup has no handle.

explain: 찻잔은 차를 마실 때 쓰는 잔이에요. 커피는 '커피잔', 물은 '컵'이나 '물잔'이라고 해서 마시는 것에 따라 이름이 달라요. 소리 나는 대로 [차짠]이라고 읽어요.

phrases.example: 그 논란은 찻잔 속의 태풍으로 끝났어요.
phrases.en: That controversy ended as a storm in a teacup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 떠들썩해 보였지만 작은 범위 안에서만 일어나고 끝난 소동을 말해요. 뉴스나 신문에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a fuss that looked big but stayed within a small circle and then faded. Common in news and newspapers.

explain_en: A 찻잔 is the cup you drink tea from. Coffee goes in a '커피잔' and water in a '컵' or '물잔', so the name changes with the drink. It is read as [차짠].

examples.en: You could at least have said goodbye before leaving.

examples.ko: 하다못해 물 한 잔이라도 드시고 가세요.
examples.en: Please have at least a glass of water before you go.

examples.ko: 돈이 없으면 하다못해 라면이라도 같이 먹어요.
examples.en: If you have no money, let's at least eat ramen together.
You should have at least sent one text message.
That store didn't have even tissues.
Please at least buy an umbrella at a convenience store.

explain: '더 큰 건 못 해도 이 정도는'이라는 아쉬움이나 불만이 들어 있어요. 뒤에 '-라도/-이라도'가 자주 와요. 단순히 '적어도'라고 말할 때보다 감정이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It carries a feeling of regret or complaint, meaning even if you can't do more, at least this much. It is often followed by '-라도/-이라도'. It is more emotional than a plain '적어도'.

examples.ko: 여행 가기 전에 은행에서 돈을 환전했어요.
examples.en: I exchanged money at the bank before the trip.
Exchanging money at the airport has high fees.
I want to exchange won for dollars.
Where can I exchange money?

examples.ko: 남은 외국 돈을 한국 돈으로 환전해 주세요.
examples.en: Please exchange my leftover foreign money into Korean money.
Changing the money took a long time, so I was late.

explain: '환전하다'는 나라가 다른 돈끼리 바꿀 때만 써요. 같은 나라 돈을 잔돈으로 바꿀 때는 '바꾸다'나 '교환하다'라고 해요. '돈을 바꿔 주세요'도 환전소에서 자연스럽게 통해요.
explain_en: '환전하다' is only for swapping money between different currencies. Breaking a bill into smaller notes is '바꾸다' or '교환하다'. At an exchange counter, '돈을 바꿔 주세요' also works naturally.

en: to be poor; to be bad; to be inferior

examples.en: The design of this bag is a bit tacky.

examples.ko: 후진 가게인 줄 알았는데 음식이 맛있었어요.
examples.en: I thought it was a shabby place, but the food was good.

examples.ko: 방이 너무 후져서 오래 못 있겠어요.
examples.en: The room is so shabby that I can't stay long.
I'm worried my outfit will look shabby.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 겉은 후지고 속은 깨끗해요.
examples.en: That restaurant looks shabby outside but is clean inside.

examples.ko: 어제 본 영화는 특수 효과가 정말 후졌어요.
examples.en: The special effects in the movie I saw yesterday were really lousy.

explain: '후지다'는 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 구어체예요. 어른이나 처음 만난 사람 앞에서는 '별로예요', '수준이 낮아요'처럼 부드럽게 말해요. 사람에게 직접 쓰면 무례하게 들려요.
explain_en: '후지다' is casual spoken Korean for friends. With elders or people you've just met, soften it with '별로예요' (it's not great) or '수준이 낮아요' (the quality is low). Said directly about a person, it sounds rude.

examples.en: When parking, you have to reverse slowly.
A truck is backing up in a narrow alley.
Check whether someone is behind you before you reverse.
I was startled when the car suddenly backed up.
I bumped lightly into the wall while backing up.

examples.ko: 초보 운전자는 후진할 때 많이 긴장해요.
examples.en: New drivers get very nervous when reversing.

explain: '후진하다'는 차가 뒤로 가는 것에 쓰고, 반대로 앞으로 가는 건 '전진하다'예요. 운전할 때 '기어를 후진에 놓다'처럼 명사로도 써요. '후진국'의 '후진'은 뒤처졌다는 뜻이라 문맥으로 구별해요.
explain_en: 후진하다 is for a vehicle going backward, and its opposite is 전진하다 (going forward). While driving you also hear it as a noun, like 기어를 후진에 놓다. The 후진 in 후진국 means lagging behind, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: I went to a recreational forest with my family on the weekend.

examples.ko: 이 휴양림은 숲속 통나무집에서 잘 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this forest retreat, you can stay in a log cabin in the woods.
I took a walk every morning in the forest retreat.
I bought a ticket at the entrance of the forest retreat.
I searched for a nearby forest retreat and looked for a place to stay.

examples.ko: 휴양림의 공기가 정말 맑아서 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: The air in the forest retreat is really clean, so I feel great.

explain: '자연휴양림'이라는 이름으로 많이 불러요. 산책만 하는 공원과 달리, 숲에서 머물며 쉬는 곳이라는 느낌이 강해요. 여행 계획이나 주말 나들이 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is often called '자연휴양림'. Unlike a park for just walking, it suggests a forest where you stay and relax. You often hear it when people talk about trips and weekend outings.
